brief: UBS sales desk (Rebecca Cheong, Nov 9) argues systematic positioning has washed out, turning the setup bullish. Risk Control exposure fell to 55%, the lowest since the tariff selloff; after the two prior comparable washouts (55% on Aug 6 2024, 30% on Apr 10 2025) the S&P 500 rose 17% and 24% over the following four months. CTA equity exposure is negative at -5%, which UBS calls a bottoming signal given real-money investors are not selling. Because the downside feedback loop is largely removed, systematic funds are unlikely to amplify further declines, so news-driven selloffs should stay shallow, helped by retail, foreign and buyback demand (buybacks return next week). UBS expects the S&P 500 to grind higher with at least 10% upside over three months. Same-day flow is cited as confirmation: $34bn bought in the S&P 500, $60bn in the Nasdaq, foreign and leveraged ETFs buying into semis and tech, and a short squeeze in UBS's short basket, while CTAs have barely participated yet but have buy triggers stacked above current levels on ES1 and RTY1. Multi-strat funds cut risk overnight on a realized-vol spike, and estimated Risk Control selling today is well below its $85-115bn daily capacity.
